items.question: How should the yogi visualize the wheel from trishula onward?
premises: The yogi visualizes the wheel.
The sequence begins at trishula.
The sequence reaches fifty ara.
items.inference: Visualization moves from trishula through the ara sequence to fifty ara.
uncertainties: Compound catuṣpañcārakakramāt may be parsed as instrumental or ablative.
items.plain_english: Thus, from trishula onward, by the four-five-ara sequence up to fifty ara, the yogi should visualize the wheel.

items.question: Which wheel forms may the undivided mind meditate upon?
premises: The mind is undivided.
The wheel may have sixty-four hundred ara.
The wheel may have thousand ara.
items.inference: Meditation may take several wheel forms, including countless thousand ara.
uncertainties: sahasrāramathāpi is treated as one token in the supplied list.
items.plain_english: Or the sixty-four-hundred-ara wheel, or the thousand-ara wheel, or the countless-thousand-ara wheel, the one of undivided mind should meditate.

items.question: What calculation exists for the great lord of world-power?
premises: The lord of consciousness is great.
The god's consciousness arises.
No calculation exists.
items.inference: For the great lord of world-power, no calculation exists.
uncertainties: devasyollāsisaṃvidaḥ may be a sandhi compound with ambiguous boundaries.
items.plain_english: Of the great lord of consciousness, of the god of arising consciousness, there is no calculation at all of the great lord of world-power.

items.question: What did Sri Srikantha explain in the auspicious scripture?
premises: His powers are the whole world.
The power-holder is the great lord.
Sri Srikantha explained this.
items.inference: The scripture states that powers are the world and the power-holder is the great lord.
uncertainties: śaktimāṃstu is treated as a supplied token, not split.
items.plain_english: His powers are the whole world; the power-holder is the great lord. Thus, in the auspicious scripture, Sri Srikantha explained.

items.question: Who explained this first-means meditation and to whom?
premises: This is first-means-form meditation.
Sri Shambhunatha explained it.
Sri Sumatiprabhu was pleased to him.
items.inference: Sri Shambhunatha explained the first-means meditation, and Sri Sumatiprabhu was pleased.
uncertainties: tuṣṭastasmai may be read as dative or locative in context.
items.plain_english: Thus this first-means-form meditation was explained by Sri Shambhunatha; to me, Sri Sumatiprabhu was pleased to him.

items.question: How should other meditations be approached by this same direction?
premises: Other meditations should be resorted to.
They reach the burden of unexcelled means.
They approach without sequence.
items.inference: By this same direction, other meditations are resorted to and reach unexcelled means without sequence.
uncertainties: anayaiva diśānyāni may be read as one compound or phrase.
items.plain_english: By this same direction, other meditations too should be resorted to, those that reach the burden of the unexcelled means without sequence.

items.question: What is explained about breath and what follows from it?
premises: Breath's function beginning with prana is explained.
By that means we speak.
We speak unexcelled expansion.
items.inference: Because breath's function is explained, by that means unexcelled expansion is spoken.
uncertainties: brūmo@nuttarapravikāsanam is treated as one supplied token.
items.plain_english: Now, breath's function, beginning with prana, is explained; by that means we speak of unexcelled expansion.

items.question: What should be visualized from rest in mere void?
premises: One is situated in own bliss.
One is in the heart.
From rest in mere void, visualize blissless.
items.inference: From rest in mere void, one should visualize the blissless state.
uncertainties: pramātraṃśamātre is an unusual compound and its exact sense is uncertain.
items.plain_english: Situated formerly in the heart in own bliss, in the measure of knower and object, from rest in mere void, one should visualize the blissless.

items.question: What should be visualized at breath rising in the object?
premises: At breath rising, in the object, visualize supreme bliss.
There one is freed.
Filling endless object parts with apana frees.
items.inference: At breath rising in the object, one should visualize supreme bliss and be freed by filling endless object parts with apana.
uncertainties: tatrānantaprameyāṃśapūraṇāpānanirvṛtaḥ is a long compound with uncertain internal grouping.
items.plain_english: At breath rising, in the object, one should visualize supreme bliss; there, freed by filling endless object parts with apana.

items.question: How does one stand in supreme bliss and become freed?
premises: One stands in supreme bliss.
One is adorned by the apana moon.
Then one is freed by single contact of endless shining objects.
items.inference: Standing in supreme bliss adorned by the apana moon, one becomes freed by single contact of endless shining objects.
uncertainties: Both supplied tokens are long compounds and may contain multiple sandhi boundaries.
items.plain_english: Standing in supreme bliss, adorned by the apana moon, then one is freed by the single contact of endless shining objects.

items.question: What happens after reaching the samana level?
premises: Having reached the samana level, one becomes full of brahma bliss.
Then one is intent on swallowing.
The mass of knower-known calculation is swallowed.
items.inference: After reaching the samana level, one becomes full of brahma bliss and then intends to swallow the mass of knower-known calculation.
uncertainties: mānameyaughakalanāgrāsatatparaḥ is a long compound with uncertain internal grouping.
items.plain_english: Having reached the samana level, one becomes full of brahma bliss; then also one is intent on swallowing the mass of knower-known calculation.

items.question: What should be visualized while resting in udana fire?
premises: Resting in udana fire, one should visualize great bliss.
There, having reached rest, one becomes calm.
One becomes calm in that great flame.
items.inference: While resting in udana fire, one should visualize great bliss and become calm in that great flame.
uncertainties: śāmyatyasminmahārciṣi is treated as one supplied token.
items.plain_english: Resting in udana fire, one should visualize great bliss; there, having reached rest, one becomes calm in that great flame.
